en: || Dhanalakṣmī Stotra ||
Dhanadā said:
Having approached her beloved god, the blue-throated Śiva,
Pārvatī, out of compassion, spoke to Śaṅkara, the source of mercy.
The Goddess said:
"O Beloved, tell me the means for crushing poverty that grants wealth instantly to virtuous householders who are destitute."
Śiva said:
While worshipping her, Maheśvara spoke these words to Pārvatī: "O Mother of the World, what you have said is appropriate, for you possess compassion for all living beings."
Having prostrated before Rāma, who is accompanied by Sītā, his younger brother, the son of Añjanā, and his followers,
I shall recite this supreme hymn that brings forth the highest bliss.
It bestows wealth upon those who have faith, makes [the goal] easily attainable immediately, and provides security and well-being; it is truth, my word is indeed the truth.
By reciting it oneself or causing others to recite it, even by the best of Brahmins who are firm believers in the sacred truths,
the acquisition of wealth occurs swiftly and poverty comes to an end.
For the sake of prosperity, he prayed as he desired to that auspicious Kalpalatā of devotion, which arises from the earth and its parts,
and which takes the form of a wish-fulfilling cow (Kāmadhenu).
O Goddess, giver of wealth, giver of wealth, you who are generous by nature and full of compassion! Be gracious, O Great Sovereign, for the sake of that which I pray for!
O Earth, beloved of the immortals, meritorious, auspicious, and worshipped by the Giver of Wealth;
O you who possess excellent wealth, grant prosperity quickly to the sacrificer!
O You who are delightful, dear to Rudra, whose form is beauty, whose nature is like that of Rāma, and who are fond of Rati;
O You whose form is the mind of the friend of the peacock (the Sun), be gracious toward me who am prostrate before You.
O you whose lotus-feet are slightly reddened, who bestow all goals and perfections;
O divine one, clad in celestial garments and adorned with divine garlands!
To her who is endowed with all virtues, marked by every auspicious sign,
whose face is like the autumn moon, who is dark blue, and whose eyes are like blue lotuses.

O Mother Bhagavatī, who possesses the beautiful beauty of a swarm of bees, whose curls are like a necklace of pearls, who is intoxicated, and whose voice is the nectar of the sweet warbling of the cuckoo!
O You who remove the anxieties of Your devotees with divine smiles and glances; O You who are the vessel of beauty, loveliness, youth, compassion, and all virtues!
In that abode of the earth, the sustainer of dharma, which was manifested by Rudra, where the lotus-like hands shine with playful grace and jingling bracelets and anklets.
O Mother, O Ambika of the universe, grant wealth to the sacrificer— a means solely for the practice of dharma— and bestow it upon me without delay.
Out of compassion, O auspicious one, fulfill my prayer;
O Earth, you who are the embodiment of wealth, you who are honored by Indra, grant me riches.
O giver of wealth, grant boons to the sacrificer; O bestower of boons, be gracious!
O Pārvatī, Śiva, and Śaṅkara, who are worthy of worship by the Brahmanas devoted to the Veda!
This hymn pacifies poverty and disease and bestows great wealth; O Śaṅkara, who brings prosperity and grants fortune, be gracious toward me, your servant.
O Lord of the Gods, those who shall recite with faith or cause others to recite with devotion this work uttered by the servants [of Śiva] through the grace of Pārvatīśa—
A gain of wealth amounting to a thousand, ten thousand, or a hundred thousand will surely come to pass.
Homage to you, O Giver of Wealth, and to the Lord of the Nidhipadma treasure!
By your grace, may I possess the abundance of wealth, grain, and other riches.
Thus ends the Śrī Dhanalakṣmī Stotra in its entirety.
